responsibility: Provides rustc’s backend-agnostic SSA code generation layer: it defines the common crate surface and persistent codegen result model in `lib.rs`, the backend trait contract in `traits`, and the shared orchestration that lowers monomorphized Rust into backend IR, packages compiled modules, and drives native artifact production for concrete backends such as LLVM. Within that role, `base.rs` supplies the core compilation workflow and shared utilities for compiling monomorphized items, scheduling codegen-unit work, choosing optimization settings, and computing output metadata; `common.rs` defines the low-level SSA abstractions and helper routines used across backends; `mono_item.rs` gives monomorphized items the shared logic for predefinition and emission; `mir` performs the main lowering of monomorphized MIR into SSA operations, including constants, places, control flow, intrinsics, and integration of debug info and coverage; `glue.rs` computes runtime size and alignment information for unsized types so backends can generate correct drop and layout-sensitive code; `meth.rs` provides trait-object method and vtable generation support; `target_features.rs` implements parsing, validation, and query support for target-feature annotations and effective feature sets; `coverageinfo` builds the LLVM-compatible coverage mapping data emitted during instrumentation; `debuginfo` provides shared policies for debugger type naming and representation choices; `back` handles the post-codegen backend pipeline, including codegen-unit and LTO coordination, metadata/object packaging, archive and linker support, runtime path computation, exported-symbol calculation, and final linking; and `errors.rs` centralizes diagnostics for these shared SSA codegen tasks. Together, these modules make `rustc_codegen_ssa` the compiler layer that bridges type-checked, monomorphized Rust and concrete backend implementations, so rustc can emit optimized objects, libraries, debuginfo, coverage data, and final linked artifacts in a backend-independent way.
